A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UltraEdit and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Corresponding content can be reliably matched despite journal reformatting and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: V2 reports original editing experiments, ablations, scalability evaluations, dataset analyses, and post-edit capability measurements, including Tables 2–4 and 11–16.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices, with a small revision to Table 2.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Eqs. (1)–(7) retain the same feature extraction, running normalization, gradient scaling, and regularized least-squares update. V3 expands the rationale without establishing a changed editing procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate zsRE, FEVER, WikiBigEdit, UltraEditBench, and UnKE supplemented with AKEW unrelated instances. SST, MMLU, MRPC, and NLI capability evaluations are also retained. No additional dataset or tested scenario appears.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain FT, MEND, MEMIT, MALMEN, RECT, WISE, PRUNE, AlphaEdit, and RLEdit. Removing the explanation for excluding MoKE and SMEdit does not change comparator membership: neither was evaluated in v2.

E3.justification: Reported edit counts, model configurations, training-data budgets, batch sizes, metrics, and final-model evaluation remain unchanged. WILD names the existing LLM-as-judge evaluation; its DeepSeek-V3.1 judge, template, and 512-token limit are retained. Omitted control descriptions do not establish an altered procedure.

E4.justification: V2 Appendix D.3 briefly reports that varying edit order has little performance impact; v3 Appendix B.3 omits this qualitative sensitivity finding. The ablations, scalability analyses, capability tests, and Table 17 cases remain. New Appendix C.4 discusses failure mechanisms without adding tested cases.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Averaging the ablation results across three backbone models remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises RLEdit’s LLaMA-3 FEVER efficacy/generalization/specificity from 91.38/89.93/41.98 to 94.03/90.67/68.71. The corresponding efficacy/generalization difference entries change from +5.80/+4.71 to +3.15/+3.97. UltraEdit’s scores, other numerical result rows, and plotted results remain unchanged; no rerun explanation is supplied.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds a substantial theoretical justification connecting normalization to MEMIT/AlphaEdit covariance preservation. It introduces approximate identity covariance, bounded-conditioning claims, a reduction from generalized to ordinary least squares, and projection guarantees. V2 contains no corresponding argument, and v3 supplies no formal proof establishing the required conditions.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain training-, subject-, and memory-free editing, lifelong normalization, over sevenfold editing speed, approximately fourfold VRAM reduction, and a benchmark supporting evaluation up to two million edits. Abstract wording changes preserve these claimed capabilities.

C2.justification: V3 substantially expands mechanistic interpretation, including an explanation of MRPC gains through regularization and semantic invariance. It adds gradient-localization failure conditions, malicious-editing implications, and explicit limitations concerning zsRE-only LLM judging and corresponding validation after two million edits. V2’s limitations mainly concern computational constraints on baseline and model scaling.

D1.justification: V3 removes the specification that epsilon is machine epsilon and the assurances that selected samples are distinct and all methods use the same edit order. Hardware, learning rate, editable-module settings, training-data allocations, and code/dataset access links remain available and unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds Gu et al. (2026) to hypernetwork-related work and removes several references, including Rebuilding ROME, LoRA, DAFNET, MoKE, and SMEdit. It also newly positions normalization as a surrogate for covariance preservation in MEMIT/AlphaEdit, while retaining the same three-paradigm research framing.

P1.justification: V3 rewrites selected introduction and method paragraphs, introduces WILD terminology, and reorganizes appendices A–F into A–D. Limitations move into the main text, while standalone reproducibility and LLM-use statements disappear. Most experimental prose and the overall narrative sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The journal format changes presentation throughout: a new title/author block, running headers, wider text and table blocks, and extensive resizing and repositioning of figures and tables. Table 2’s caption clarifies equal-budget versus large-scale rows. All nine figures and seventeen tables are retained.

improvement.justification: Clearer comparison labels and more specific limitations are useful, but v3 introduces unsupported technical guarantees. Its new Section 3.2 argument treats standardization as covariance whitening and assumes normalized H, whereas the retained procedure explicitly uses unnormalized H in the least-squares update. This weakens the theoretical justification relative to v2. Together with omitted reproducibility details and essentially unchanged empirical support, these problems outweigh the limited clarification gains.
